customManagers.description: Swift releases. swiftlang/swift tags them swift-X.Y.Z-RELEASE. Version and commit are captured by ONE regex so Renovate moves them together -- build.sh asserts the clone of SWIFT_TAG is exactly SWIFT_SHA, so a version bumped without its commit fails closed. SWIFT_TAG derives from SWIFT_VERSION, so there is no third literal to leave behind.

The Mavergreen/swift-toolchain release supplying the host build environment. Trackable at all only because build.sh now verifies both assets against that release's own published SHA256SUMS: the hand-pasted BUILDSUPPORT_SHA256/TOOLCHAIN_SHA256 it replaces could not be updated by a bot, which is why this pin sat at 6.3.3-mavericks.1 while swift-toolchain shipped .3. The versioning regex reads -mavericks.N as the build number: Renovate's default versioning coerces it away, so .1 and .4 compared equal and the pin stayed at .1 even after it became trackable.

packageRules.description: EXCEPTION to the family ship-if-green default. A MINOR or MAJOR Swift bump is not self-contained here: TOOLCHAIN_REF must move to a swift-toolchain release built for that Swift, which no regex can infer. The six source patches are cut against specific stdlib and runtime internals, so a bump that happens to build proves nothing about the 10.9 behaviour a macOS 26 runner cannot see. Needs a human. A PATCH bump takes the family default.
